messages:
maria: quick notes from today's live-run of the "fast-lane" speculative pipeline on rwd-14b-4bit. ran against 2K mixed prompts (chat + docs). end-to-end throughput up ~1.5x vs fp16 baseline, median latency improved ~25ms. p99 tail shows intermittent spikes (~70ms) correlated with node evictions. overall regen churn ~1.1%.
kevin: nice. what's the spec strategy (window, scorer, fallback budget)?
maria: primary = spec model (4bit qkv-permute layout), spec-window=10 tokens, safety-net scorer fp16 checks after window, scorer threshold = 3.5 (logprob delta), fallback budget = 40 tokens. scorer runs on same-AZ device to avoid cross-AZ hop.
sara: were these runs with batching? impact on spec window behavior?
maria: batch=12 for main runs. batching increases throughput but made scorer bursts more expensive. small batches (4) reduced p99 but lowered overall TPS ~12%.
kevin: any visible bias from quantization? token frequency shifts, reply length?
maria: small shift: -2.7% rare token usage on spec path, average reply length unchanged. human spot-check (n=60) found 3 cases with mild hallucination / factual drift that triggered fallback; 1 case slipped through where scorer delta was 2.9 (just under threshold).
oliver: infra noise noted: two pod restarts at T+00:18. I filtered warmup, but some spikes persisted post-filter.
maria: I added runtime tags to traces: node_id, gpu_mem_util, scorer_latency. will upload traces to s3://rwd-spec-traces/1719456789/ for deeper triage.
kevin: what command + config did you use? paste please.
maria: ```
# runner snippet
python live_spec_runner.py \
  --model rwd-14b-4bit-fastlane \
  --verify-model rwd-14b-fp16 \
  --spec-window 10 \
  --scorer-threshold 3.5 \
  --fallback-budget 40 \
  --batch 12 \
  --eval-file data/mix_prompts_v3.jsonl
```
maria: scorer config (light): scorer_device=cuda:2, scorer_batch=48, score_metric=logprob_delta
sara: can we try an ensemble-lite scorer (two lightweight heads average) to catch overconfident mispreds?
maria: queued an ensemble-lite ablation: spec-window variants [6,10,14] x scorer-thresholds [2.5,3.5,5.0] x scorer-mode [single,ensemble-lite]. job ids in notebook.
kevin: how are you defining regen? token-level or sequence-level?
maria: sequence-level final-output-diff vs fp16 reference, plus token-KL across full sequence. regen (seq) = 1.1%, avg token-KL = 0.018.
oliver: deployment plan? sounds canary-worthy for Dedicated.
maria: propose 3% traffic to canary pool on Dedicated: route try-fastlane in local cheap pool, on fallback route to fp16 pool in same AZ. add masking to avoid cross-AZ fallback. set watchlist in Console: regen-rate, p99 latency delta, scorer-latency, and user-facing error rate. alert thresholds: regen > 2.5% OR p99 > baseline+120ms -> rollback.
sara: add a small hourly holdout re-eval (200 prompts) capturing diffs and human tags. also export a compact diff summary to metrics-store.
maria: done. outputs go to s3 + we emit a summary metric: spec.regen_hourly and spec.kld_hourly.
kevin: curious about cost math. does 1.5x throughput translate to unit-cost savings after scorer overhead?
maria: measured token-cost reduction ~27% net (spec path cheap tokens >> scorer overhead). variance depends on scorer frequency; we expect ~20-30% savings for similar quality.
oliver: can we shunt scorer to a cheaper GPU type (lower mem) to save cost while keeping latency?
maria: possibly — tester job will probe scorer_device=cuda:4 (lower spec) and a cpu-fallback for very small scorer-batches.
maria: immediate next steps: run ablations, trial ensemble-lite scorer, tighten alerting, and start 3% canary in Dedicated once ablation confirms regen <2%. deploy-bot: canary start?
deploy-bot: deploy started: rwd-fastlane-canary v0.1 -> 3 replicas (initiated by maria).
maria: TL;DR: promising perf wins, small targeted quality regressions concentrated in overconfident edge-cases. ablations queued, canary rolling with strict alerts. :rocket:
